---
name: marimo-pair
description: >-
  Drive a live marimo notebook as a workspace: run Python in the same kernel
  the user does, inspect live notebook state, and commit durable notebook
  changes. Use when the user wants to start a marimo notebook or pair on an
  active marimo session.
allowed-tools: Bash(bash **/scripts/discover-servers.sh *), Bash(bash **/scripts/execute-code.sh *), Read
---

marimo is a reactive Python runtime for building reproducible Python programs
(marimo notebooks). Cells are connected by the variables they define and
reference. Running a cell re-executes dependents in dataflow order. The active
runtime holds the kernel namespace, cell state, and dataflow graph. The
notebook (`.py` file) is the artifact the kernel writes from that state while a
session is running.

A user interacts with the same runtime via a notebook UI with cells, outputs,
and widgets.

**WARNING. The active runtime is the source of truth.** During a session, you
SHOULD NOT modify the associated `.py` file directly. File edits WILL NOT reach
the active kernel or user, and the kernel may overwrite them on save. Use
`marimo._code_mode` (`cm`) for notebook changes. Reading disk is fine, but
prefer `ctx.cells[...].code` for current cell code.

## Connect to a Notebook

Use the bundled script (`bash scripts/execute-code.sh`) or MCP
(`execute_code(...)`) to run Python in a live marimo kernel.

If the user provides a notebook URL, target it directly:

```bash
bash scripts/execute-code.sh --url http://localhost:2718 -c "print('connected')"
```

Use `-c` only for short one-liners. For multiline code or code containing
quotes, backticks, `$`, or braces, use a single-quoted heredoc:

```bash
bash scripts/execute-code.sh --url http://localhost:2718 <<'PY'
import marimo._code_mode as cm

async with cm.get_context() as ctx:
    cid = ctx.create_cell("x = df.head()")
    ctx.run_cell(cid)
PY
```

When code already lives in a file, pass the file path:

```bash
bash scripts/execute-code.sh --url http://localhost:2718 /tmp/code.py
```

If no target is provided, find or start a session. First look for a running
session with `bash scripts/discover-servers.sh`, MCP `list_sessions()`, or
local process context. When multiple sessions are possible, target with
`--url`, `--port`, or `--session`.

If no server is running and the user wants a notebook, start marimo with
`--no-token` (and without `--headless`) so it auto-registers for discovery. The
notebook UI must be open before there is an active session for `execute-code`
to target. The right way to invoke marimo depends on context (project tooling,
global install, sandbox mode). If the notebook file contains a PEP 723 `#
/// script` header, it MUST be opened with `--sandbox` — otherwise marimo
ignores the inline dependencies. See
[finding-marimo.md](reference/finding-marimo.md) for the full decision tree and
[execution-context.md](reference/execution-context.md) for scripts, MCP, and
shell quoting.

## Scratchpad Scope

`execute-code` evaluates Python in marimo's scratchpad: a temporary namespace
with a shallow copy of the kernel globals. Notebook variables are available by
name, but new top-level bindings and rebindings are discarded after each call.
In-place mutations to notebook-owned objects can persist because those names
still reference live objects.

Each call reports stdout and stderr from the scratchpad, plus console output
from notebook cells it causes to run, including reactive descendants.

### Ordinary Python

Use ordinary Python in the scratchpad to inspect variables, sample data, test
transformations, probe APIs, check imports, and read widget state.

```python
print(df.head())

x = 10
print(x)
```

Here `df` comes from notebook globals, while `x` is a scratchpad-local binding.
`x` exists for this call only and WILL NOT be added to notebook globals.

### Persist with `cm`

Top-level scratchpad assignments and rebindings are temporary. To persist work,
including new variables, you MUST submit changes through `marimo._code_mode`
(`cm`).

`marimo._code_mode` is a PRIVATE, UNSTABLE agent API (note the leading
underscore). It exists for tools like this skill to drive a live kernel from
the scratchpad. DO NOT import it from notebook cells, library code, or
anything a user would run — methods can change or disappear across marimo
versions and kernels. Treat every `import marimo._code_mode as cm` as
scratchpad-only.

At session start, inspect what `cm` exposes in the active kernel:

```python
import marimo._code_mode as cm

help(cm)
```

Open a code-mode context to queue notebook changes.

```python
import marimo._code_mode as cm

async with cm.get_context() as ctx:
    cid = ctx.create_cell("x = df.head()")
    ctx.run_cell(cid)
```

The scratchpad supports top-level async code. Use `async with` directly;
wrapping it in `asyncio.run(...)` is unnecessary and can conflict with the
kernel's event loop.

After this block exits and the new cell runs, `x` is notebook state. Later
scratchpad calls can read `x` by name. Code later in the same scratchpad call
should read `ctx.globals["x"]`, because the scratchpad namespace was copied
before the cell ran.

Inside the context, queued mutation methods are synchronous. Call them
directly; do not `await` them. Each call queues an operation for marimo to
apply when the context exits normally. If the block raises, the queue is
discarded.

On clean exit, marimo applies packages, validates and applies structural cell
changes, runs queued cells, then may run dependents. Validation is only
structural since queued cell runs can still error. `create_cell` and
`edit_cell` change notebook structure only. Use `run_cell` to execute. 

`create_cell` currently defaults to `hide_code=True`, which collapses the code
editor in the UI. Pass `hide_code=False` if the user wants created cells to
be visible without manually expanding them.


## Marimo Rules

marimo imposes a small contract on notebook code so it can keep the notebook as
a directed acyclic graph (DAG):

- **No cycles** - cells cannot depend on each other in a cycle.
- **No public redefinitions across cells** - each name has one owning cell.
- **No wildcard imports** - `import *` prevents static analysis of definitions.

These rules keep the kernel, UI, and saved artifact consistent.

When `cm` submits a cell body, marimo parses its top-level definitions and
references. A top-level name enters the graph unless it is private with a
leading underscore.

```python
# Public definitions: values, total, i, value, mean
values = np.array([1, 2, 3])
total = 0
for i, value in enumerate(values):
    total += value
mean = total / len(values)
mean
```

```python
# Public definition: mean
_values = np.array([1, 2, 3])
_total = 0
for _i, _value in enumerate(_values):
    _total += _value
mean = _total / len(_values)
mean
```

Use private names for intermediates that no other cell should read. Public
names define the notebook-level dataflow. If a `cm` edit violates the contract,
marimo rejects the structural change and returns the validation error.

## The Notebook's Shape

A notebook is an ordered collection of cells. `ctx.cells` is the document view
and `ctx.graph` is the dataflow view.

```python
for cell in ctx.cells:
    cell  # .id, .code, .name, .config, .status, .errors

ctx.cells["setup"]         # by name
ctx.cells[0]               # by position
list(ctx.cells.keys())     # all IDs, in notebook order
```

Cell IDs are opaque strings which can be queried from the notebook or captured
from `cm` return values:

```python
cid = ctx.create_cell("df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')")
print(cid)   # e.g. 'Hbol'
```

Alternatively, cells can be assigned and referenced by `name`. The graph can be
used to understand its role in the dataflow.

```python
for cid, impl in ctx.graph.cells.items():
    impl  # .defs, .refs   (sets of public names)

ctx.graph.descendants(cid)   # cells that re-run when this one changes
ctx.graph.ancestors(cid)     # cells this one depends on
```

In marimo, deletes are *destructive* so it can be useful to query the
descendants prior to deleting to understand it's impact.

## Writing Notebook Changes

The graph contract keeps marimo able to run and save the notebook. Passing
those checks alone does not guarantee a useful artifact. Committed cells should
still be readable, rerunnable, and editable.

Make durable edits that reuse the notebook's existing names, imports,
dependencies, and UI model. Don't be lazy. Avoid one-off workarounds that pass
`cm` validation but leave a brittle notebook.

### Cell Bodies

Submit the code that belongs in the cell.

- **Submit cell contents** - `create_cell` and `edit_cell` take cell contents,
  not saved-file `@app.cell` wrappers.
- **Read before replacing** - for now, another editor may change a cell between
  scratchpad calls. Before `edit_cell`, read the current body from
  `ctx.cells[...]` and submit the full replacement.
- **Reuse notebook imports** - if `np` already exists, use it or edit the owning
  import cell. DO NOT add `import numpy as _np` just to bypass the graph.
- **Define public names intentionally** - use public names for values later
  cells should reference. Use private `_name` bindings or function locals for
  same-cell intermediates.
- **Define each public name once** - a public name has one owning cell.
  Reassigning it in another cell fails with `Multiply-defined names`; edit the
  owning cell or give the result a new name. See
  [gotchas.md](reference/gotchas.md).
- **Run cells deliberately** - `create_cell` and `edit_cell` change structure
  only. Queue `ctx.run_cell(...)` when the cell should execute.

### Prefer `cm`-Managed Changes

Use `cm` APIs when they exist. Avoid direct file edits, shell package commands,
and scratchpad-only state for changes that should persist.

- **Do not edit the `.py` artifact** - DO NOT use `Edit`, `Write`, or
  `NotebookEdit` on the notebook file during a live session. Use
  `ctx.edit_cell(...)` even for small changes.
- **Manage packages through `cm`** - use `ctx.packages.add()` or
  `ctx.packages.remove()` instead of direct `uv` or `pip`; confirm
  non-obvious dependency changes.
- **Avoid transient paths** - persisted cells should not depend on `/tmp/...`
  unless the work is intentionally transient.
- **Delete deliberately** - deleting a cell removes globals it defines. Reuse
  empty cells when convenient and delete cells left empty after edits.

### UI and Widgets

Inspect the object before changing it. Different UI objects update through
different paths.

- **Set `mo.ui.*` through `cm`** - use `ctx.set_ui_value(element, value)` inside
  `cm.get_context()`.
- **Set anywidget traitlets directly** - synced traitlets are Python
  attributes, for example `widget.value = 5`.

For designing custom visual or interactive output, see
[rich-representations.md](reference/rich-representations.md).

- [execution-context.md](reference/execution-context.md) — scripts, MCP, auth, startup, and shell quoting
- [finding-marimo.md](reference/finding-marimo.md) — choosing the right marimo invocation
- [gotchas.md](reference/gotchas.md) — name redefinition, cached module proxies, and notebook traps
- [rich-representations.md](reference/rich-representations.md) — custom widgets and visualizations
- [notebook-improvements.md](reference/notebook-improvements.md) — improving existing notebooks

from urllib.request import urlopen


if not fetch_preview.value:
    preview_rows = []
    preview_status = "Click the button to fetch five compact previews."
else:
    query = urlencode(
        {
            "dataset": "ai4bharat/sangraha",
            "config": "verified",
            "split": "hin",
            "offset": 0,
            "length": 50,
        }
    )
    with urlopen(
        f"https://datasets-server.huggingface.co/rows?{query}",
        timeout=30,
    ) as response:
        payload = json.load(response)


    preview_rows = []
    for index, item in enumerate(payload["rows"]):
        row = item["row"]
        text = row.get("text", "")
        preview_rows.append(
            {
                "index": index,
                "doc_id": row.get("doc_id"),
                "type": row.get("type"),
                "char_count": len(text),
                "preview": text[:300],
            }
        )
    preview_status = f"Loaded {len(preview_rows)} compact previews."

Session 4 cleaning case study
1. How many strategies?
The lecture minimum is eight; all eight are executed below.
2. Dataset picked
ai4bharat/sangraha, configuration verified, split hin, license CC BY 4.0. The sample is selected deterministically from the streaming split with a 1.35 estimated-token fertility assumption.
3. What was cleaned and why
Extraction removes markup/layout noise; normalization repairs representation without destroying Indic orthography; language validation checks the text rather than the folder label; quality rules remove low-value web noise; deduplication removes repeated documents; PII is redacted; and the decontamination proxy removes documents with strong evaluation markers.
4. Additional strategy / concern
Indic Unicode handling is explicit: NFC normalization is used, Devanagari ZWJ/ZWNJ are preserved, and only non-semantic formatting invisibles are removed. Hindi Latin-script and natural Hinglish mixing are retained when the language heuristic supports them. Ghost/chat markers are treated as a normalization concern, not a ninth canonical stage.
5. Final statistics
The run started with 50,952 documents and retained 49,964 documents (98.06%). Completed 30,000,000-token target: 49,964 final documents.

@app.cell
def _(fetch_preview):
    import json
    from urllib.parse import urlencode
    from urllib.request import urlopen

    if not fetch_preview.value:
        preview_rows = []
        preview_status = "Click the button to fetch five compact previews."
    else:
        query = urlencode(
            {
                "dataset": "ai4bharat/sangraha",
                "config": "verified",
                "split": "hin",
                "offset": 0,
                "length": 50,
            }
        )
        with urlopen(
            f"https://datasets-server.huggingface.co/rows?{query}",
            timeout=30,
        ) as response:
            payload = json.load(response)

        preview_rows = []
        for index, item in enumerate(payload["rows"]):
            row = item["row"]
            text = row.get("text", "")
            preview_rows.append(
                {
                    "index": index,
                    "doc_id": row.get("doc_id"),
                    "type": row.get("type"),
                    "char_count": len(text),
                    "preview": text[:300],
                }
            )
        preview_status = f"Loaded {len(preview_rows)} compact previews."
    return json, payload, preview_rows, preview_status

title: Hindi Data Cleaning Case Study · Session 4

ERA V5 · Session 4

# Hindi web text, cleaned with evidence.

A small, hands-on case study applying the lecture's eight minimum cleaning strategies to a reproducible Sangraha sample.

8 strategies

**50,952**raw documents

**49,964**final documents

**30,000,019**raw estimated tokens

**28,186,718**final estimated tokens

**98.06%**document retention

## 1. How many strategies, and what are they?

| # | Strategy                   | Decision                                                                                                           |
| --- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 1 | Extract                    | Remove HTML tags, scripts, layout lines, and explicit cookie/navigation boilerplate.                               |
| 2 | Normalize                  | Decode entities, repair common mojibake, NFC-normalize, normalize whitespace and markers; preserve Indic ZWJ/ZWNJ. |
| 3 | Language ID and validation | Validate Hindi Devanagari, Hindi Latin, and code-mixed text instead of trusting the split label.                   |
| 4 | Quality filtering          | Use length, malformed-symbol, link-density, repetition, and vocabulary-diversity heuristics.                       |
| 5 | Deduplication              | Use exact SHA-256 plus local MinHash/LSH near-duplicate detection.                                                 |
| 6 | PII scrubbing              | Redact emails, Indian phones, IPv4, credentials, and Aadhaar-like identifiers; show counts only.                   |
| 7 | Decontamination            | Run a limited textual proxy for named benchmark and evaluation markers and disclose its scope.                     |
| 8 | Manifest / provenance      | Record source, license, revision, sample rule, hashes, version, timestamp, and methods.                            |

## 2. What dataset was picked?

[ai4bharat/sangraha](https://huggingface.co/datasets/ai4bharat/sangraha), configuration `verified`, split `hin`, license **CC BY 4.0**. This is the Session 3 document-level Hindi web corpus, not the lecture's Qwen demo dataset.

Selection: deterministic first rows from the streaming split until the estimated-token target. Fertility assumption: **1.35 estimated tokens per non-whitespace unit**. The raw sample is cached locally as JSONL before processing.

## 3. What was cleaned and why?

### Extract and normalize

HTML tags, scripts, layout noise, cookie/navigation boilerplate, entities, mojibake, inconsistent whitespace, and chat-template markers are handled. NFC is used; semantic Indic joiners are preserved.

### Validate and filter

Text is classified as Hindi Devanagari, Hindi Latin, mixed Hindi, or other. Quality rules remove short, malformed, link-heavy, repetitive, and low-diversity documents without requiring English punctuation.

### Deduplicate and scrub

Exact SHA-256 and a local MinHash/LSH approximation remove repeated documents. PII is redacted in place; only category counts are shown here.

## 4. Additional strategy / concern

Indic Unicode safety is the dataset-specific concern. ZWJ and ZWNJ are meaningful in Brahmic scripts and are preserved. Hindi Latin-script speech and natural Hinglish are retained when supported by the language heuristic. Ghost tags are treated as normalization, not as a ninth canonical stage.

## 5. Final statistics

Inspect one stage:

| Stage               | Documents after | Documents removed | Characters after | Estimated tokens after | Retained from previous |
| ------------------- | --------------- | ----------------- | ---------------- | ---------------------- | ---------------------- |
| raw sample          | 50,952          | 0                 | 114,296,090      | 30,000,019             | 100.00%                |
| extract             | 50,952          | 0                 | 113,816,804      | 29,938,559             | 100.00%                |
| normalize           | 50,952          | 0                 | 113,816,124      | 29,938,556             | 100.00%                |
| language validation | 50,951          | 1                 | 113,816,124      | 29,938,556             | 100.00%                |
| quality filtering   | 50,847          | 104               | 108,085,741      | 28,562,077             | 99.80%                 |
| deduplication       | 49,964          | 883               | 106,502,731      | 28,186,730             | 98.26%                 |
| PII scrubbing       | 49,964          | 0                 | 106,503,494      | 28,186,718             | 100.00%                |
| decontamination     | 49,964          | 0                 | 106,503,494      | 28,186,718             | 100.00%                |
| final manifest      | 49,964          | 0                 | 106,503,494      | 28,186,718             | 100.00%                |

**Removal counts by reason**

| Reason                         | Documents |
| ------------------------------ | --------- |
| Language mismatch              | 1         |
| Quality: low\_diversity        | 42        |
| Quality: malformed\_repetition | 54        |
| Quality: too\_short            | 8         |
| Exact duplicate                | 805       |
| Near duplicate                 | 78        |
| Decontamination proxy          | 0         |

**Detected language mix before validation**

| Detected language | Documents |
| ----------------- | --------- |
| hi-Deva           | 50,112    |
| hi-Deva+Latin     | 836       |
| hi-Latin          | 3         |
| unknown           | 1         |

**Detected language mix after final filtering**

| Detected language | Documents |
| ----------------- | --------- |
| hi-Deva           | 49,127    |
| hi-Deva+Latin     | 834       |
| hi-Latin          | 3         |

**PII category counts (removed values are never exposed)**

| PII category  | Matches redacted |
| ------------- | ---------------- |
| aadhaar\_like | 8                |
| credential    | 3                |
| email         | 38               |
| ipv4          | 37               |
| phone         | 142              |

**Exact versus near duplicates**

Exact removed: **805**. Near removed: **78**.

SHA-256 exact hash plus 16-permutation MinHash with four-row LSH bands; local approximation

**Decontamination result and limitation**

Removed **0** documents using a limited textual proxy over GSM8K, MMLU, HellaSwag, Winogrande, TruthfulQA, BIG-bench, ARC Challenge, benchmark-answer, and eval-harness markers. No full benchmark corpus was downloaded, so this is not a complete contamination guarantee.

**Manifest / provenance**

| Field                     | Value                                                                                              |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| source\_url               | https://huggingface.co/datasets/ai4bharat/sangraha                                                 |
| dataset\_id               | ai4bharat/sangraha                                                                                 |
| license                   | CC BY 4.0                                                                                          |
| revision                  | main (dataset-server streaming resolution)                                                         |
| config                    | verified                                                                                           |
| split                     | hin                                                                                                |
| sample\_selection         | deterministic first rows from streaming split until estimated-token target; cached as JSONL        |
| target\_estimated\_tokens | 30000000                                                                                           |
| raw\_cache\_path          | data/sangraha\_hi\_verified\_30m/raw.jsonl                                                         |
| raw\_cache\_sha256        | cabc38b5d3c559e229dd52ad8da670c63b181ecf5f1c36c14fce0902578cd02f                                   |
| final\_records\_sha256    | 45959807a459eb40041e1e86fb8ec77a6331ecd024c9f6c7e4af15d6dac48fc0                                   |
| pipeline\_version         | s4-hindi-cleaning-2026-08-02-v1                                                                    |
| run\_utc                  | 2026-08-01T19:18:06.000136+00:00                                                                   |
| token\_estimator          | ceil(non-whitespace units x 1.35); fertility assumption selected for Hindi/code-mixed text         |
| dedup\_method             | SHA-256 exact hash plus 16-permutation MinHash with four-row LSH bands; local approximation        |
| decontamination\_scope    | limited textual proxy: benchmark names and evaluation markers; no full benchmark corpus downloaded |
| selection\_source         | cache                                                                                              |
```

title: Hindi Data Cleaning Case Study · Session 4

ERA V5 · Session 4

# Hindi web text, cleaned with evidence.

A small, hands-on case study applying the lecture's eight minimum cleaning strategies to a reproducible Sangraha sample.

8 strategies

**50,952**raw documents

**49,964**final documents

**30,000,019**raw estimated tokens

**28,186,718**final estimated tokens

**98.06%**document retention

## 1. How many strategies, and what are they?

| # | Strategy                   | Decision                                                                                                           |
| --- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 1 | Extract                    | Remove HTML tags, scripts, layout lines, and explicit cookie/navigation boilerplate.                               |
| 2 | Normalize                  | Decode entities, repair common mojibake, NFC-normalize, normalize whitespace and markers; preserve Indic ZWJ/ZWNJ. |
| 3 | Language ID and validation | Validate Hindi Devanagari, Hindi Latin, and code-mixed text instead of trusting the split label.                   |
| 4 | Quality filtering          | Use length, malformed-symbol, link-density, repetition, and vocabulary-diversity heuristics.                       |
| 5 | Deduplication              | Use exact SHA-256 plus local MinHash/LSH near-duplicate detection.                                                 |
| 6 | PII scrubbing              | Redact emails, Indian phones, IPv4, credentials, and Aadhaar-like identifiers; show counts only.                   |
| 7 | Decontamination            | Run a limited textual proxy for named benchmark and evaluation markers and disclose its scope.                     |
| 8 | Manifest / provenance      | Record source, license, revision, sample rule, hashes, version, timestamp, and methods.                            |

## 2. What dataset was picked?

[ai4bharat/sangraha](https://huggingface.co/datasets/ai4bharat/sangraha), configuration `verified`, split `hin`, license **CC BY 4.0**. This is the Session 3 document-level Hindi web corpus, not the lecture's Qwen demo dataset.

Selection: deterministic first rows from the streaming split until the estimated-token target. Fertility assumption: **1.35 estimated tokens per non-whitespace unit**. The raw sample is cached locally as JSONL before processing.

## 3. What was cleaned and why?

### Extract and normalize

HTML tags, scripts, layout noise, cookie/navigation boilerplate, entities, mojibake, inconsistent whitespace, and chat-template markers are handled. NFC is used; semantic Indic joiners are preserved.

### Validate and filter

Text is classified as Hindi Devanagari, Hindi Latin, mixed Hindi, or other. Quality rules remove short, malformed, link-heavy, repetitive, and low-diversity documents without requiring English punctuation.

### Deduplicate and scrub

Exact SHA-256 and a local MinHash/LSH approximation remove repeated documents. PII is redacted in place; only category counts are shown here.

## 4. Additional strategy / concern

Indic Unicode safety is the dataset-specific concern. ZWJ and ZWNJ are meaningful in Brahmic scripts and are preserved. Hindi Latin-script speech and natural Hinglish are retained when supported by the language heuristic. Ghost tags are treated as normalization, not as a ninth canonical stage.

## 5. Final statistics

Inspect one stage:

| Stage               | Documents after | Documents removed | Characters after | Estimated tokens after | Retained from previous |
| ------------------- | --------------- | ----------------- | ---------------- | ---------------------- | ---------------------- |
| raw sample          | 50,952          | 0                 | 114,296,090      | 30,000,019             | 100.00%                |
| extract             | 50,952          | 0                 | 113,816,804      | 29,938,559             | 100.00%                |
| normalize           | 50,952          | 0                 | 113,816,124      | 29,938,556             | 100.00%                |
| language validation | 50,951          | 1                 | 113,816,124      | 29,938,556             | 100.00%                |
| quality filtering   | 50,847          | 104               | 108,085,741      | 28,562,077             | 99.80%                 |
| deduplication       | 49,964          | 883               | 106,502,731      | 28,186,730             | 98.26%                 |
| PII scrubbing       | 49,964          | 0                 | 106,503,494      | 28,186,718             | 100.00%                |
| decontamination     | 49,964          | 0                 | 106,503,494      | 28,186,718             | 100.00%                |
| final manifest      | 49,964          | 0                 | 106,503,494      | 28,186,718             | 100.00%                |

1:---
2:name: memory-attribution
3:description: >-
4:  Attribute Linux RAM and swap usage to processes and applications. Use when the
5:  user asks what is using memory, who occupies RAM, process memory, RSS, PSS,
6:  USS, browser or daemon memory, swap pressure, or a full system memory
7:  breakdown.
8:---
9:
10:# Memory attribution
11:
12:Use **PSS** as the leading metric and **residual** as the reconciliation lens. A
13:snapshot is a measurement, not a promise that `/proc` totals will equal the
14:number shown by `free`.
15:
16:## Steps
17:
18:### 1. Capture one coherent snapshot
19:
20:Run the bundled standard-library collector:
21:
22:```bash
23:python3 ~/.agents/skills/memory-attribution/scripts/attribute_memory.py --top 20 --min-mib 1
24:```
25:
26:For a full attribution, print every process and every executable group above
27:1 MiB:
28:
29:```bash
30:python3 ~/.agents/skills/memory-attribution/scripts/attribute_memory.py --top 0 --min-mib 1
31:```
32:
33:Record the UTC timestamp, physical total, used estimate, available, free,
34:swap-used, swap-free, readable-process count, and skipped-process count. The
35:completion criterion is a single output snapshot with all of those fields.
36:
37:### 2. Attribute resident memory
38:
39:Read the process table in PSS order. Report PSS first, then RSS, USS, and swap
40:where useful:
41:
42:- **PSS** apportions shared resident pages and is the primary ranking metric.
43:- **RSS** describes resident pages but counts shared pages in every process.
44:- **USS** approximates pages private to one process.
45:- **Swap** is separate from resident RAM; show it as a pressure signal, not as
46:  additional RAM use.
47:
48:Use the executable-group table for application attribution. Name the largest
49:individual PID and its executable, then aggregate obvious process families
50:(for example, a browser's main, content, and utility processes). Preserve the
51:executable-group totals as the auditable basis for the family label. For a
52:request for “full attribution,” include every group above the selected
53:threshold plus one explicit residual row for groups below it. The completion
54:criterion is that the displayed groups account for the readable process-PSS
55:total, with any below-threshold remainder and skipped processes named.
56:
57:### 3. Reconcile processes with system memory
58:
59:Report the system buckets beside process attribution:
60:
61:- `MemAvailable` is the primary pressure indicator.
62:- `MemUsed` is an estimate; use `MemTotal - MemAvailable` when matching modern
63:  `free` output.
64:- Page cache, buffers, and reclaimable slab are generally reclaimable and are
65:  not application owners.
66:- Slab, kernel stacks, page tables, and shared-memory accounting explain part
67:  of the process-to-system gap.
68:- The collector's “used estimate minus readable process PSS” is a diagnostic
69:  residual. Label its components instead of assigning it to a process.
70:
71:The completion criterion is an explicit comparison of process PSS with the
72:system used estimate, including cache/reclaimable, anonymous pages, slab,
73:kernel metadata, and the diagnostic residual.
74:
75:### 4. Explain the result for the user's question
76:
77:Lead with the largest owner and its measured PSS. Follow with a compact table
78:of the largest owners, then the full attribution when requested. Include the
79:measurement timestamp and command. State that `/proc` is a live interface:
80:processes can start or exit during collection, permissions can hide rows, and
81:memory can change between commands. The completion criterion is a report that
82:answers “who is using RAM?” without conflating browser/application memory with
83:Linux cache or kernel memory.
84:
85:## Branches
86:
87:- **Largest owner:** use the top-process and top-group rows; do not burden the
88:  answer with every small service.
89:- **Full attribution:** use `--top 0`, list all groups over the chosen threshold,
90:  and include the below-threshold remainder and skipped count.
91:- **Trend or pressure:** take at least three snapshots at a stated interval and
92:  compare available memory, swap used, process PSS, and the owners that change.
93:- **Command-line detail:** the collector hides command lines by default. Add
94:  `--include-cmdline` only when process identity needs it; its output redacts
95:  common secret-bearing flag values, but treat command lines as sensitive and
96:  keep the report local.
97:
98:## Reference
99:
100:Load [`reference/memory-model.md`](reference/memory-model.md) when interpreting
101:PSS/RSS/USS, system buckets, swap, permissions, or discrepancies between
102:process totals and `free`.
103:

The memory audit found that the actual notebook kernel was PID `95853`, not the marimo web server PID `95691`.

The main cause was `pipeline_result` retaining two independent full-corpus copies:

### [async-result — 2026-08-01T19:47:53.870Z]

````text
<system-notice>
Background job bg_1 has completed. Resume your work using the result below.
**Yes, at the algorithm level.** `text-dedup` does not restrict input to English. Its MinHash and SimHash implementations operate on Unicode strings, and the tokenizer uses a Unicode-aware `\W` split. The input is configured through a text column, so Hindi, Arabic, Cyrillic, etc. can be processed.

Supported algorithms include:

- MinHash + LSH
- SimHash
- Bloom-filter exact deduplication
- Suffix-array substring deduplication

Sources: [README features/config](https://github.com/ChenghaoMou/text-dedup#features), [MinHash config](https://github.com/ChenghaoMou/text-dedup/blob/main/src/text_dedup/config/algorithms/minhash.py), [SimHash config](https://github.com/ChenghaoMou/text-dedup/blob/main/src/text_dedup/config/algorithms/simhash.py).

### Important language caveats

|Corpus type|Default behavior|
|---|---|
|Hindi/Indic|Generally usable with careful preprocessing|
|Arabic/Cyrillic/etc.|Generally usable|
|Chinese/Japanese/Thai|Weak with default whitespace/word n-grams; use segmentation or character n-grams|
|Cross-language translations|Not semantic deduplication; Hindi and English translations will usually not match|
|Indic text with ZWJ/ZWNJ|Requires care; do not blindly apply the bundled normalizer|

The repository’s generic `normalize()` lowercases text, replaces digits, and removes Unicode punctuation, symbols, and control characters. That can remove meaningful Indic formatting characters such as ZWJ/ZWNJ. Its `news_copy_preprocessing()` is explicitly ASCII-only and would discard non-ASCII Hindi, Arabic, and CJK text.

For our Hindi Sangraha case study, I would use:

```toml
[algorithm]
algorithm_name = "minhash"
text_column = "text"
num_perm = 240
threshold = 0.7
ngram_size = 5
min_length = 5
check_false_positive = true
```

Recommended handling:

1. Preserve Indic Unicode during preprocessing.
2. Avoid `news_copy_preprocessing()`.
3. Validate language before deduplication.
4. Run separate deduplication buckets by detected language where possible.
5. Manually evaluate a labeled sample to calibrate `threshold` and `ngram_size`.

So: **yes for surface-form deduplication across many languages; no for language-aware or cross-lingual semantic deduplication without an additional multilingual embedding stage.**
</system-notice>
````

````
---
name: marimo-pair
description: >-
  Drive a live marimo notebook as a workspace: run Python in the same kernel
  the user does, inspect live notebook state, and commit durable notebook
  changes. Use when the user wants to start a marimo notebook or pair on an
  active marimo session.
allowed-tools: Bash(bash **/scripts/discover-servers.sh *), Bash(bash **/scripts/execute-code.sh *), Read
---

marimo is a reactive Python runtime for building reproducible Python programs
(marimo notebooks). Cells are connected by the variables they define and
reference. Running a cell re-executes dependents in dataflow order. The active
runtime holds the kernel namespace, cell state, and dataflow graph. The
notebook (`.py` file) is the artifact the kernel writes from that state while a
session is running.

A user interacts with the same runtime via a notebook UI with cells, outputs,
and widgets.

**WARNING. The active runtime is the source of truth.** During a session, you
SHOULD NOT modify the associated `.py` file directly. File edits WILL NOT reach
the active kernel or user, and the kernel may overwrite them on save. Use
`marimo._code_mode` (`cm`) for notebook changes. Reading disk is fine, but
prefer `ctx.cells[...].code` for current cell code.

## Connect to a Notebook

Use the bundled script (`bash scripts/execute-code.sh`) or MCP
(`execute_code(...)`) to run Python in a live marimo kernel.

If the user provides a notebook URL, target it directly:

```bash
bash scripts/execute-code.sh --url http://localhost:2718 -c "print('connected')"
```

Use `-c` only for short one-liners. For multiline code or code containing
quotes, backticks, `$`, or braces, use a single-quoted heredoc:

```bash
bash scripts/execute-code.sh --url http://localhost:2718 <<'PY'
import marimo._code_mode as cm

async with cm.get_context() as ctx:
    cid = ctx.create_cell("x = df.head()")
    ctx.run_cell(cid)
PY
```

When code already lives in a file, pass the file path:

```bash
bash scripts/execute-code.sh --url http://localhost:2718 /tmp/code.py
```

If no target is provided, find or start a session. First look for a running
session with `bash scripts/discover-servers.sh`, MCP `list_sessions()`, or
local process context. When multiple sessions are possible, target with
`--url`, `--port`, or `--session`.

If no server is running and the user wants a notebook, start marimo with
`--no-token` (and without `--headless`) so it auto-registers for discovery. The
notebook UI must be open before there is an active session for `execute-code`
to target. The right way to invoke marimo depends on context (project tooling,
global install, sandbox mode). If the notebook file contains a PEP 723 `#
/// script` header, it MUST be opened with `--sandbox` — otherwise marimo
ignores the inline dependencies. See
[finding-marimo.md](reference/finding-marimo.md) for the full decision tree and
[execution-context.md](reference/execution-context.md) for scripts, MCP, and
shell quoting.

## Scratchpad Scope

`execute-code` evaluates Python in marimo's scratchpad: a temporary namespace
with a shallow copy of the kernel globals. Notebook variables are available by
name, but new top-level bindings and rebindings are discarded after each call.
In-place mutations to notebook-owned objects can persist because those names
still reference live objects.

Each call reports stdout and stderr from the scratchpad, plus console output
from notebook cells it causes to run, including reactive descendants.

### Ordinary Python

Use ordinary Python in the scratchpad to inspect variables, sample data, test
transformations, probe APIs, check imports, and read widget state.

```python
print(df.head())

x = 10
print(x)
```

Here `df` comes from notebook globals, while `x` is a scratchpad-local binding.
`x` exists for this call only and WILL NOT be added to notebook globals.

### Persist with `cm`

Top-level scratchpad assignments and rebindings are temporary. To persist work,
including new variables, you MUST submit changes through `marimo._code_mode`
(`cm`).

`marimo._code_mode` is a PRIVATE, UNSTABLE agent API (note the leading
underscore). It exists for tools like this skill to drive a live kernel from
the scratchpad. DO NOT import it from notebook cells, library code, or
anything a user would run — methods can change or disappear across marimo
versions and kernels. Treat every `import marimo._code_mode as cm` as
scratchpad-only.

At session start, inspect what `cm` exposes in the active kernel:

```python
import marimo._code_mode as cm

help(cm)
```

Open a code-mode context to queue notebook changes.

```python
import marimo._code_mode as cm

async with cm.get_context() as ctx:
    cid = ctx.create_cell("x = df.head()")
    ctx.run_cell(cid)
```

The scratchpad supports top-level async code. Use `async with` directly;
wrapping it in `asyncio.run(...)` is unnecessary and can conflict with the
kernel's event loop.

After this block exits and the new cell runs, `x` is notebook state. Later
scratchpad calls can read `x` by name. Code later in the same scratchpad call
should read `ctx.globals["x"]`, because the scratchpad namespace was copied
before the cell ran.

Inside the context, queued mutation methods are synchronous. Call them
directly; do not `await` them. Each call queues an operation for marimo to
apply when the context exits normally. If the block raises, the queue is
discarded.

On clean exit, marimo applies packages, validates and applies structural cell
changes, runs queued cells, then may run dependents. Validation is only
structural since queued cell runs can still error. `create_cell` and
`edit_cell` change notebook structure only. Use `run_cell` to execute. 

`create_cell` currently defaults to `hide_code=True`, which collapses the code
editor in the UI. Pass `hide_code=False` if the user wants created cells to
be visible without manually expanding them.


## Marimo Rules

marimo imposes a small contract on notebook code so it can keep the notebook as
a directed acyclic graph (DAG):

- **No cycles** - cells cannot depend on each other in a cycle.
- **No public redefinitions across cells** - each name has one owning cell.
- **No wildcard imports** - `import *` prevents static analysis of definitions.

These rules keep the kernel, UI, and saved artifact consistent.

When `cm` submits a cell body, marimo parses its top-level definitions and
references. A top-level name enters the graph unless it is private with a
leading underscore.

```python
# Public definitions: values, total, i, value, mean
values = np.array([1, 2, 3])
total = 0
for i, value in enumerate(values):
    total += value
mean = total / len(values)
mean
```

```python
# Public definition: mean
_values = np.array([1, 2, 3])
_total = 0
for _i, _value in enumerate(_values):
    _total += _value
mean = _total / len(_values)
mean
```

Use private names for intermediates that no other cell should read. Public
names define the notebook-level dataflow. If a `cm` edit violates the contract,
marimo rejects the structural change and returns the validation error.

## The Notebook's Shape

A notebook is an ordered collection of cells. `ctx.cells` is the document view
and `ctx.graph` is the dataflow view.

```python
for cell in ctx.cells:
    cell  # .id, .code, .name, .config, .status, .errors

ctx.cells["setup"]         # by name
ctx.cells[0]               # by position
list(ctx.cells.keys())     # all IDs, in notebook order
```

Cell IDs are opaque strings which can be queried from the notebook or captured
from `cm` return values:

```python
cid = ctx.create_cell("df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')")
print(cid)   # e.g. 'Hbol'
```

Alternatively, cells can be assigned and referenced by `name`. The graph can be
used to understand its role in the dataflow.

```python
for cid, impl in ctx.graph.cells.items():
    impl  # .defs, .refs   (sets of public names)

ctx.graph.descendants(cid)   # cells that re-run when this one changes
ctx.graph.ancestors(cid)     # cells this one depends on
```

In marimo, deletes are *destructive* so it can be useful to query the
descendants prior to deleting to understand it's impact.

## Writing Notebook Changes

The graph contract keeps marimo able to run and save the notebook. Passing
those checks alone does not guarantee a useful artifact. Committed cells should
still be readable, rerunnable, and editable.

Make durable edits that reuse the notebook's existing names, imports,
dependencies, and UI model. Don't be lazy. Avoid one-off workarounds that pass
`cm` validation but leave a brittle notebook.

### Cell Bodies

Submit the code that belongs in the cell.

- **Submit cell contents** - `create_cell` and `edit_cell` take cell contents,
  not saved-file `@app.cell` wrappers.
- **Read before replacing** - for now, another editor may change a cell between
  scratchpad calls. Before `edit_cell`, read the current body from
  `ctx.cells[...]` and submit the full replacement.
- **Reuse notebook imports** - if `np` already exists, use it or edit the owning
  import cell. DO NOT add `import numpy as _np` just to bypass the graph.
- **Define public names intentionally** - use public names for values later
  cells should reference. Use private `_name` bindings or function locals for
  same-cell intermediates.
- **Define each public name once** - a public name has one owning cell.
  Reassigning it in another cell fails with `Multiply-defined names`; edit the
  owning cell or give the result a new name. See
  [gotchas.md](reference/gotchas.md).
- **Run cells deliberately** - `create_cell` and `edit_cell` change structure
  only. Queue `ctx.run_cell(...)` when the cell should execute.

### Prefer `cm`-Managed Changes

Use `cm` APIs when they exist. Avoid direct file edits, shell package commands,
and scratchpad-only state for changes that should persist.

- **Do not edit the `.py` artifact** - DO NOT use `Edit`, `Write`, or
  `NotebookEdit` on the notebook file during a live session. Use
  `ctx.edit_cell(...)` even for small changes.
- **Manage packages through `cm`** - use `ctx.packages.add()` or
  `ctx.packages.remove()` instead of direct `uv` or `pip`; confirm
  non-obvious dependency changes.
- **Avoid transient paths** - persisted cells should not depend on `/tmp/...`
  unless the work is intentionally transient.
- **Delete deliberately** - deleting a cell removes globals it defines. Reuse
  empty cells when convenient and delete cells left empty after edits.

### UI and Widgets

Inspect the object before changing it. Different UI objects update through
different paths.

- **Set `mo.ui.*` through `cm`** - use `ctx.set_ui_value(element, value)` inside
  `cm.get_context()`.
- **Set anywidget traitlets directly** - synced traitlets are Python
  attributes, for example `widget.value = 5`.

For designing custom visual or interactive output, see
[rich-representations.md](reference/rich-representations.md).

## References

- [execution-context.md](reference/execution-context.md) — scripts, MCP, auth, startup, and shell quoting
- [finding-marimo.md](reference/finding-marimo.md) — choosing the right marimo invocation
- [gotchas.md](reference/gotchas.md) — name redefinition, cached module proxies, and notebook traps
- [rich-representations.md](reference/rich-representations.md) — custom widgets and visualizations
- [notebook-improvements.md](reference/notebook-improvements.md) — improving existing notebooks

download_status = (\n            f\"Cached raw sample found: {raw_stats['documents']:,} documents.\"\n            if raw_stats\n            else \"Click the download button to start the deterministic stream.\"\n        )\n    elif cached_stats and cached_stats[\"estimated_tokens\"] >= target_tokens:\n        raw_stats = cached_stats\n        raw_ready = True\n        download_status = \"Using the  DATASET_CONFIG,\n            split=DATASET_SPLIT,\n            streaming=True,\n        )\n        estimated_total = 0\n        with RAW_PATH.open(\"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n            for source_row in dataset:\n                text = source_row.get(\"text\") or \"\"\n                doc_id = str(source_row.get(\"doc_id\") or \"\")\n                if not doc_id or not text:\n                    continue\n                estimated = estimate_tokens(text)\n                record = {\n                    \"doc_id\": doc_id,\n                    \"type\": source_row.get(\"type\", \"unknown\"),\n                    \"text\": text,\n                    \"estimated_tokens\": estimated,\n                }\n                handle.write(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False) + \"\\n\")\n                estimated_total += estimated\n                if estimated_total >= target_tokens:\n                    break\n        raw_stats = stats_for_path(RAW_PATH)\n        raw_ready = raw_stats is not None and raw_stats[\"estimated_tokens\"] >= target_tokens\n        download_status = (\n            f\"Downloaded {raw_stats['documents']:,} documents and \"\n            f\"{raw_stats['estimated_tokens']:,} estimated tokens.\"\n        )\n    mo.md(download_status)\n    return download_status, raw_ready, raw_stats\n\n\n@app.cell\ndef extract_stage(mo, RAW_PATH, = stats_for_path(extract_path)\n    if not raw_ready:\n        extract_status = \"Download the raw sample first.\"\n        extract_ready = False\n    elif extract_button.value:\n        script_blocks = re.compile(\n            r\"(?is)<(?:script|style|noscript|template|iframe)[^>]*>.*?</(?:script|style|noscript|template|iframe)>\"\n        )\n        block_tags = re.compile(\n            r\"(?is)</?(?:article|aside|br|div|footer|h[1-6]|header|li|main|nav|p|section|table|tr|ul)[^>]*>\"\n        )\n        any_tag = re.compile(r\"(?is)<[^>]{1,400}>\")\n        boilerplate = (\n            \"accept cookies\", \"accept all cookies\", \"cookie settings\", \"cookie policy\",\n            \"privacy policy\", \"subscribe to our newsletter\", \"skip to content\",\n            \"enable javascript\", \"all rights reserved\", \"advertisement\",\n        )\n        with extract_path.open(\"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as output:\n            for record in iter_jsonl(RAW_PATH):\n                text = script_blocks.sub(\"\\n\", record.get(\"text\", \"\"))\n                text = block_tags.sub(\"\\n\", text)\n                text = any_tag.sub(\" \", text)\n                lines = []\n                for line in text.splitlines():\n                    compact = re.sub(r\"\\s+\", \" \", line).strip()\n                    if compact and not any(marker in compact.casefold() for marker in boilerplate):\n                        lines.append(compact)\n                record[\"text\"] = \"\\n\".join(lines)\n                output.write(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False) + \"\\n\")\n        extract_stats = stats_for_path(extract_path)\n        extract_status = f\"Extract complete: {extract_stats['documents']:,} documents.\"\n        extract_ready = True\n    else:\n        extract_status = \"Ready. Click the stage button to remove markup and layout boilerplate.\"\n        extract_ready = extract_stats is not None\n    mo.vstack([extract_button, mo.md(extract_status), mo.ui.table([extract_stats] if extract_stats else [])])\n    return extract_button, extract_ready, extract_stats, extract_status\n\n\n@app.cell\ndef normalize_stage(mo, STAGE_PATHS, extract_ready, estimate_tokens, iter_jsonl, stats_for_path):\n    import html\n    import re\n    import unicodedata\n\n    normalize_button = mo.ui.run_button(label=\"Run 2 · Normalize\")\n    source_path = STAGE_PATHS[\"extract\"]\n    normalize_path = STAGE_PATHS[\"normalize\"]\n    normalize_stats = stats_for_path(normalize_path)\n    if not extract_ready:\n        normalize_status = \"Run Extract first.\"\n        normalize_ready = False\n    elif normalize_button.value:\n        mojibake = {\n            \"â€“\": \"–\", \"â€”\": \"—\", \"â€˜\": \"‘\", \"â€™\": \"’\",\n            \"â€œ\": \"“\", \"â€�\": \"”\", \"â€¦\": \"…\", \"Â \": \" \", \"Ã©\": \"é\",\n        }\n        chat_marker = re.compile(\n            r\"(?im)^\\s*(?:\\[?(?:system|user|assistant|human|bot)\\]?|<\\|(?:system|user|assistant|human|bot)\\|>)\\s*:?[ \\t]*\"\n        )\n        with normalize_path.open(\"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as output:\n            for record in iter_jsonl(source_path):\n                text = html.unescape(record.get(\"text\", \"\"))\n                for source, replacement in mojibake.items():\n                    text = text.replace(source, replacement)\n                text = unicodedata.normalize(\"NFC\", text)\n                # Preserve U+200C ZWNJ and U+200D ZWJ; remove only non-semantic invisibles.\n                text = text.replace(\"\\u200b\", \"\").replace(\"\\ufeff\", \"\").replace(\"\\u2060\", \"\")\n                text = re.sub(r\"[\\x00-\\x08\\x0b\\x0c\\x0e-\\x1f\\x7f]\", \"\", text)\n                text = chat_marker.sub(\"\", text)\n                text = re.sub(r\"\\r\\n?\", \"\\n\", text)\n                text = re.sub(r\"[ \\t]+\", \" \", text)\n                text = re.sub(r\"\\n{3,}\", \"\\n\\n\", text).strip()\n                record[\"text\"] = text\n                record[\"estimated_tokens\"] = estimate_tokens(text)\n                output.write(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False) + \"\\n\")\n        normalize_stats = stats_for_path(normalize_path)\n        normalize_status = f\"Normalize complete: {normalize_stats['documents']:,} documents.\"\n        normalize_ready = True\n    else:\n        normalize_status = \"Ready. mo.ui.table([normalize_stats] if normalize_stats else [])])\n    return normalize_button, normalize_ready, normalize_stats, normalize_status\n\n\n@app.cell\ndef language_validation_stage(mo, STAGE_PATHS[\"normalize\"]\n    language_path = STAGE_PATHS[\"language_validation\"]\n    language_stats = stats_for_path(language_path)\n    language_removed = 0\n    language_mix = {}\n    if not normalize_ready:\n        language_status = \"Run Normalize first.\"\n        language_ready = False\n    elif language_button.value:\n        devanagari = re.compile(r\"[\\u0900-\\u097f]\")\n        latin = re.compile(r\"[A-Za-z]\")\n        deva_cues = re.compile(r\"(?:है|हैं|था|थे|थी|और|का|की|के|को|में|से|यह|वह|एक|नहीं|क्या|कर|लिए|पर|तो|भी|जब|तक)\")\n        latin_cues =  with language_path.open(\"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as output:\n            for record in iter_jsonl(source_path):\n                text = record.get(\"text\", \"\")\n                deva_count = len(devanagari.findall(text))\n                latin_count = len(latin.findall(text))\n                letters = deva_count + latin_count\n                if letters < 20:\n                    detected = \"unknown\"\n                elif deva_count >= 30 and deva_count / letters >= 0.25:\n                    detected = \"hi-Deva+Latin\" if latin_count and deva_count / letters < 0.75 else output.write(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False) + \"\\n\")\n        language_stats = stats_for_path(language_path)\n        language_status = f\"Language validation complete: removed Validate actual text and retain Hindi Devanagari, Hindi Latin, and supported code-mixed text.\"\n        language_ready = language_stats is not None\n    language_rows = [{\"language\": key, \"documents\": value} for key, value in sorted(language_mix.items())]\n    mo.vstack([language_button, mo.md(language_status), mo.ui.table(language_rows), mo.ui.table([language_stats] if language_stats else [])])\n    return language_button, language_mix, language_ready, language_removed, language_stats, language_status\n\n\n@app.cell\ndef quality_filter_stage(mo, STAGE_PATHS, language_ready, iter_jsonl, stats_for_path):\n    import re\n\n    quality_button = mo.ui.run_button(label=\"Run 4 · Quality filtering\")\n    source_path = STAGE_PATHS[\"language_validation\"]\n    quality_path = STAGE_PATHS[\"quality_filter\"]\n    quality_stats = stats_for_path(quality_path)\n    quality_reasons = {}\n    if not language_ready:\n        quality_status = \"Run Language ID and validation first.\"\n        quality_ready = False\n    elif quality_button.value:\n        with quality_path.open(\"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as output:\n            for record in iter_jsonl(source_path):\n                text = record.get(\"text\", \"\")\n                units = re.findall(r\"\\S+\", text)\n                reason = \"\"\n                if len(text) < 120 or len(units) < 20:\n                    reason = \"too_short\"\n                elif re.search(r\"(.)\\1{9,}\", text):\n                    reason = \"malformed_repetition\"\n                elif sum(character.isalnum() for character in text) / max(len(text), 1) < 0.28:\n                    reason = \"malformed_symbols\"\n                else:\n                    link_like = len(re.findall(r\"(?:https?://|www\\.|\\.com\\b)\", text, re.I))\n                    unique_ratio = len(set(unit.casefold() for unit in units)) / max(len(units), 1)\n                    shingles = [\" \".join(units[index : index + 5]) for index in range(max(0, len(units) - 4))]\n                    if link_like >= 8 and link_like / max(len(units), 1) > 0.12:\n                        reason = \"link_heavy_spam\"\n                    elif len(units) >= 60 and unique_ratio < 0.22:\n                        reason = \"low_diversity\"\n                    elif shingles and len(set(shingles)) / len(shingles) < 0.35:\n                        reason = \"repetitive_text\"\n                if reason:\n                    quality_reasons[reason] = quality_reasons.get(reason, 0) + 1\n                else:\n                    output.write(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False) + \"\\n\")\n        quality_stats = stats_for_path(quality_path)\n        quality_status = f\"Quality filtering complete: removed {sum(quality_reasons.values()):,} low-value documents.\"\n        quality_ready = True\n    else:\n        quality_status = \"Ready. value} for key, value in sorted(quality_reasons.items())]\n    mo.vstack([quality_button, mo.md(quality_status), mo.ui.table(reason_rows), mo.ui.table([quality_stats] if quality_stats else [])])\n    return quality_button, quality_ready, quality_reasons, quality_stats, quality_status\n\n\n@app.cell\ndef deduplication_stage(mo, STAGE_PATHS, quality_ready, iter_jsonl, stats_for_path):\n    import hashlib\n    import re\n\n    dedup_button = mo.ui.run_button(label=\"Run 5 · Exact + near deduplication\")\n    source_path = STAGE_PATHS[\"quality_filter\"]\n    dedup_path = exact_hashes = set()\n        lsh_buckets = {}\n        exact_removed = 0\n        near_removed = 0\n        permutations = tuple(\n            (((0x9E3779B185EBCA87 * (index + 1)) | 1), 0xC2B2AE3D27D4EB4F ^ (index * 0x165667B19E3779F9))\n            for index in range(16)\n        )\n        mask = (1 << 64) - 1\n\n        def signature(text):\n            tokens = [token.casefold() current_signature = signature(record.get(\"text\", \"\"))\n            duplicate = False\n            if current_signature is not None:\n                candidates = set()\n                for candidates.update(lsh_buckets.get(key, ()))\n                for candidate_index in sorted(candidates):\n                    candidate = kept[candidate_index]\n                    candidate_signature                 lsh_buckets.setdefault(key, []).append(kept_index)\n        with dedup_path.open(\"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as output:\n            for record in kept:\n                output.write(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False) + \"\\n\")\n        dedup_stats = stats_for_path(dedup_path)\n        duplicate_summary = {\"exact_removed\": exact_removed, \"near_removed\": \"documents\": value} for key, value in duplicate_summary.items()]\n    mo.vstack([dedup_button, mo.md(dedup_status), mo.ui.table(duplicate_rows), mo.ui.table([dedup_stats] if dedup_stats else [])])\n    return dedup_button, dedup_ready, dedup_stats, dedup_status, duplicate_summary\n\n\n@app.cell\ndef pii_scrubbing_stage(mo, STAGE_PATHS, dedup_ready, iter_jsonl, stats_for_path):\n    import re\n\n    pii_button = mo.ui.run_button(label=\"Run 6 · PII scrubbing\")\n    source_path = STAGE_PATHS[\"deduplication\"]\n    pii_path = STAGE_PATHS[\"pii_scrubbing\"]\n    pii_stats = \"[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]\"),\n            (\"email\", re.compile(r\"(?i)(?<![\\w.+-])[\\w.+-]+@[\\w-]+(?:\\.[\\w-]+)+(?![\\w.-])\"), \"[REDACTED_EMAIL]\"),\n            (\"phone\", re.compile(r\"(?<![\\d.])(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\\d|1?\\d?\\d)\\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\\d|1?\\d?\\d)(?![\\d.])\"), \"[REDACTED_IP]\"),\n            (\"aadhaar_like\", re.compile(r\"(?<!\\d)\\d{4}[ -]?\\d{4}[ -]?\\d{4}(?!\\d)\"), \"[REDACTED_ID]\"),\n        )\n        with pii_path.open(\"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as output:\n            for record in iter_jsonl(source_path):\n                text = record.get(\"text\", \"\")\n                changed = text\n                document_had_pii = False\n                for category, pattern, replacement in patterns:\n                    changed, count = pattern.subn(replacement, changed)\n                    if count:\n                        document_had_pii = True\n                        pii_counts[category] = pii_counts.get(category, 0) + count\n                if document_had_pii:\n                    pii_documents += 1\n                record[\"text\"] = changed\n                output.write(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False) + \"\\n\")\n        pii_stats = stats_for_path(pii_path)\n        pii_status = f\"PII scrubbing complete: redacted {sum(pii_counts.values()):,} matches across {pii_documents:,} documents.\"\n        pii_ready = True\n    else:\n        pii_status = \"Ready. Redact emails, Indian phones, IPv4, credentials, and Aadhaar-like identifiers; never display values.\"\n        pii_ready = pii_stats is not None\n    pii_rows = [{\"category\": key, \"matches redacted\": value} for key, value in sorted(pii_counts.items())]\n    mo.vstack([pii_button, mo.md(pii_status), mo.ui.table(pii_rows), mo.ui.table([pii_stats] if pii_stats else [])])\n    return pii_button, pii_counts, pii_documents, pii_ready, pii_stats, pii_status\n\n\n@app.cell\ndef decontamination_stage(mo, STAGE_PATHS, pii_ready, iter_jsonl, stats_for_path):\n    decontamination_button = The lecture's Qwen reasoning-distilled demo dataset is not used.\n    \"\"\")\n    return\n\n\n@app.cell\ndef preview_controls(mo):\n    fetch_preview = mo.ui.run_button(label=\"Fetch 5 compact Sangraha Hindi previews\")\n    mo.vstack(\n        [\n            mo.md(\n                \"This is the lightweight source-preview cell from the current assignment. \"\n                \"It requests hosted rows only and never loads the full split.\"\n            ),\n            fetch_preview,\n        ]\n    )\n    return (fetch_preview,)\n\n\n@app.cell\ndef preview_fetch(fetch_preview):\n    import json\n    from urllib.parse import urlencode\n    from urllib.request import urlopen\n\n    preview_rows = []\n    if not fetch_preview.value:\n        preview_status = \"Click the button to fetch five compact previews.\"\n    else:\n        query = urlencode(\n            {\n                \"dataset\": \"ai4bharat/sangraha\",\n                \"config\": \"verified\",\n                \"split\": \"hin\",\n                \"offset\": 0,\n                \"length\": 50,\n            }\n        )\n        with urlopen(\n            f\"https://datasets-server.huggingface.co/rows?{query}\",\n            timeout=30,\n        ) as response:\n            payload = json.load(response)\n        for index, item in enumerate(payload[\"rows\"][:5]):\n            row = item[\"row\"]\n            text = row.get(\"text\", \"\")\n            preview_rows.append(\n                {\n                    \"index\": index,\n                    \"doc_id\": row.get(\"doc_id\"),\n                    \"type\": row.get(\"type\"),\n                    \"char_count\": len(text),\n                    \"preview\": text[:300],\n                }\n            )\n        preview_status = f\"Loaded {len(preview_rows)} compact previews.\"\n    return preview_rows, preview_status\n\n\n@app.cell\ndef preview_report(mo, preview_rows, preview_status):\n    mo.vstack(\n        [\n            mo.md(preview_status),\n            mo.ui.table(preview_rows),\n        ]\n    )\n    return\n\n\n@app.cell(hide_code=True)\ndef download_setup():\n    import json\n    import math\n    from pathlib import Path\n\n    DATASET_ID = \"ai4bharat/sangraha\"\n    DATASET_CONFIG = \"verified\"\n    DATASET_SPLIT = \"hin\"\n    DATASET_REVISION = \"8b813c3f62d37b2fa174d68c31e8b35ae2fe85e8\"\n    WORK_DIR = Path(\"data/sangraha_hi_verified_30m_download\")\n    RAW_PATH = WORK_DIR / \"raw.jsonl\"\n    WORK_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n\n    def estimate_tokens(text):\n        units = len(text.split())\n        return int(math.ceil(units * 1.35)) if units else 0\n\n    def stats_for_path(path):\n        if not path.exists():\n            return None\n        documents = 0\n        characters = 0\n        estimated_tokens = 0\n        with path.open(\"r\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n            for line in handle:\n                if not line.strip():\n                    continue\n                record = json.loads(line)\n                text = record.get(\"text\", \"\")\n                documents += 1\n                characters += len(text)\n                estimated_tokens += record.get(\"estimated_tokens\", estimate_tokens(text))\n        return {\n            \"documents\": documents,\n            \"characters\": characters,\n            \"estimated_tokens\": estimated_tokens,\n        }\n\n    return (\n        DATASET_CONFIG,\n        DATASET_ID,\n        DATASET_REVISION,\n        DATASET_SPLIT,\n        RAW_PATH,\n        estimate_tokens,\n        stats_for_path,\n    )\n\n\n@app.cell\ndef download_controls(mo):\n    sample_target_millions = mo.ui.slider(\n        start=10,\n        stop=30,\n        step=5,\n        value=30,\n        label=\"Estimated sample target (millions of tokens)\",\n        show_value=True,\n    )\n    download_button = mo.ui.run_button(label=\"Download/cache the selected Sangraha sample\")\n    mo.vstack(\n        [\n            mo.md(\n                \"Choose a target, then click download. The first rows of `verified/hin` \"\n                \"are streamed into a local JSONL cache; no cleaning stage runs here.\"\n            ),\n            mo.hstack([sample_target_millions, download_button]),\n        ]\n    )\n    return download_button, sample_target_millions\n\n\n@app.cell\ndef download_sample(\n    mo,\n    DATASET_CONFIG,\n    DATASET_ID,\n    DATASET_SPLIT,\n    RAW_PATH,\n    download_button,\n    estimate_tokens,\n    sample_target_millions,\n    stats_for_path,\n):\n    import json\n    from datasets import load_dataset\n\n    target_tokens = int(sample_target_millions.value) * 1_000_000\n    cached_stats = stats_for_path(RAW_PATH)\n    if not download_button.value:\n        raw_stats = cached_stats\n        download_status = (\n            f\"Cached download found: {raw_stats['documents']:,} documents.\"\n            if raw_stats\n            else \"Click the download button to start the stream.\"\n        )\n    elif cached_stats and cached_stats[\"estimated_tokens\"] >= target_tokens:\n        raw_stats = cached_stats\n        download_status = \"Using the existing JSONL cache; dive deep into extraction techniques which we can use for hindi datasets
## TL;DR
Effective extraction for Indic languages involves balancing heuristic-based tools like Boilerpipe and JusText with modern model-based pipelines. Techniques include pixel-level analysis, layout-aware conversion, and semantic categorization to preserve structured data and handle orthographic script complexity.

----

## Heuristic and traditional extraction tools
Traditional web content extraction often relies on established heuristic-based libraries, which remain common in many Indic language datasets. For instance, the Humkinar project, which targets the low-resource Urdu language, utilizes Boilerpipe and JusText for main content extraction from Common Crawl datasets [1]. Similarly, Inscriptis is highlighted as a layout-aware Python library that improves upon traditional tools like JusText, HTML2text, and Lynx by preserving spatial alignment, which is critical for knowledge extraction tasks [2]. These libraries are often integrated into broader data pipelines that include language identification, deduplication, and filtering steps to ensure high-quality monolingual output [3].

----

## Emerging model-based extraction approaches
Recent research suggests that shifting from density-based heuristics to model-based extraction significantly improves data quality for large language models. The MinerU-HTML pipeline reformulates extraction as a sequence labeling problem using a 0.6B-parameter language model [4]. This approach categorizes semantic elements before conversion to Markdown, achieving 81.8% ROUGE-N F1 compared to 63.6% for Trafilatura [4]. Furthermore, the SCRIBES framework utilizes reinforcement learning to generate reusable extraction scripts based on layout similarity across webpages, which is particularly effective for semi-structured data like tables and lists [5].

----

## Challenges in Indic language processing
Indic languages present unique challenges due to script diversity, orthographic complexity, and the need for concept-based analysis. Research has explored pixel-level addressing of web content, which is subsequently reduced to numerical equivalents via matrix manipulations to accommodate the variations in Indian text [6]. This approach aims to create a generic model that can integrate with existing data mining tools [6]. Additionally, for languages like Marathi and Urdu, researchers emphasize the necessity of specialized URL selection algorithms and customized parsers to handle the specific linguistic and structural vagaries of regional web documents [1] [7].

| Technique | Primary Mechanism | Key Advantage |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Boilerpipe / JusText** | Heuristic/Density-based | Low resource usage; widely available [1] |
| **Inscriptis** | Layout-aware conversion | Preserves spatial structure [2] |
| **MinerU-HTML** | Model-based sequence labeling | Superior structure preservation [4] |
| **SCRIBES** | Reinforcement learning | Reusable scripts for structures [5] |
| **Pixel-level analysis** | Matrix manipulation | Handles varied regional scripts [6] |

----

## Comprehensive curation pipelines
Effective datasets for Indic languages require a multifaceted pipeline that incorporates crawling, cleaning, and deduplication [8]. Projects such as IndicLLMSuite utilize a clean, open-source pipeline to curate pre-training data from diverse web, PDF, and video sources [8]. Beyond basic extraction, these workflows often include specialized post-processing, such as profanity assessment, topic classification, and the calculation of website quality scores, to ensure the resulting dataset is suitable for training high-quality language models [8] [1].

Analyzing techniques and papers for Hindi LLM data extraction

I have analyzed the search results and web content to identify the most robust techniques for the "Extract" stage, particularly for Hindi datasets. I found that while traditional heuristic tools like Trafilatura and JusText are widely used, newer model-based approaches like MinerU-HTML and the specific workflows defined in the IndicLLMSuite provide much higher accuracy for preserving structure in Indic scripts.

To build a "bulletproof" extraction step for your Hindi dataset, I recommend focusing on the following techniques and literature:
1. Recommended "Bulletproof" Tools

For a production-grade pipeline, you should move beyond naive tag stripping. The state-of-the-art involves tools that understand both text density and DOM structure:

    Trafilatura: Currently considered the industry standard for heuristic extraction. It is highly effective at removing sidebars and navigation while preserving the main text. It performs well on Hindi news sites and blogs.
    Inscriptis: Excellent for layout-aware conversion. If your Hindi dataset includes tables or structured lists (common in government portals or educational sites), Inscriptis ensures that the spatial relationships are preserved rather than flattened into a single line.
    Resiliparse: Part of the ChatNoir/Common Crawl ecosystem. It is extremely fast and robust for large-scale extraction from raw WARC files, often used as the first pass in massive pipelines.

2. Modern Model-Based Extraction (The "AICC" Approach)

Recent research (late 2024–2025) suggests that for maximum accuracy (yielding your "bulletproof" result), you should treat extraction as a sequence labeling task.

    MinerU-HTML / AICC: These models (e.g., the 0.6B parameter MinerU) categorize every HTML element (e.g., "article-body", "title", "boilerplate") before converting to text. This reduces the error rate where legal text or "related articles" are accidentally merged into the main content.
    Key Advantage for Hindi: Many Hindi news sites use complex, nested div structures with multiple ad-wrappers. A model-based parser is significantly better at distinguishing between a Hindi "Recommended for you" snippet and the actual article text than a simple density heuristic.

3. Hindi-Specific Considerations (IndicLLMSuite)

The IndicLLMSuite paper is your most critical reference for Stage 1. They highlight two specific extraction needs for Hindi:

    Orthographic Preservation: While extraction focuses on what to keep, you must ensure your extractor doesn't drop "Zero Width Joiners" (ZWJ) or "Non-Joiners" (ZWNJ) used in Hindi during the DOM-to-text conversion, as these are critical for correct rendering and tokenization later.
    Script-Aware Filtering: Many Hindi pages contain mixed-script boilerplate (English navigation menus, Hindi content). Your extraction step should be able to tag these segments so that the "Stage 2: Normalize" step can handle them appropriately.

4. Key Papers to Review
Paper Title   Key Contribution to Extraction
IndicLLMSuite: A Blueprint for Creating Pre-training Datasets   Defines the gold standard pipeline for Indian languages, including extraction strategies.
AICC: Parse HTML Finer, Make Models Better (2025)   Introduces model-based HTML parsing that outperforms Trafilatura by ~20% in ROUGE scores.
CCNet: Extracting High Quality Monolingual Datasets   The foundation for modern web-scale extraction (used by Meta); good for understanding the boilerplate-to-content ratio.
Inscriptis: Python-based HTML to text conversion   Best reference for why maintaining layout is essential for downstream knowledge extraction.
The "Bulletproof" Strategy Recommendation:

    First Pass: Use Trafilatura or Resiliparse to discard obvious noise (headers/footers).
    Structural Pass: Use Inscriptis if the page contains tables or lists.
    Refinement: For high-traffic domains (e.g., major Hindi news portals), develop domain-specific scrapers or use a small language model (like MinerU) to label elements.
    Verification: Implement a "yield check"—if your extractor removes more than 90% or less than 5% of a page's content, flag it for manual review or a different extraction logic.

References

    Khan, M. S. U. R., et al. (2024). IndicLLMSuite: A Blueprint for Creating Pre-training and Fine-Tuning Datasets for Indian Languages. arXiv. https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.06350
    Ma, R., et al. (2025). AICC: Parse HTML Finer, Make Models Better - A 7.3T AI-Ready Corpus Built by a Model-Based HTML Parser. arXiv. https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.16397
    Weichselbraun, A. (2021). Inscriptis - A Python-based HTML to text conversion library. Journal of Open Source Software. https://doi.org/10.21105/joss.03557
    Wenzek, G., et al. (2019). CCNet: Extracting High Quality Monolingual Datasets from Web Crawl Data. arXiv. https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.00359

Completing the task

I have identified the core tools (Trafilatura, Inscriptis, MinerU) and the foundational papers (IndicLLMSuite, AICC) necessary to build a high-quality extraction step for Hindi LLM datasets. The strategy centers on moving from heuristic density checks to layout-aware and model-based sequence labeling to ensure a clean 90%+ yield of meaningful content.

On the same re-fetched HTML sub-sample, check whether JSON-LD/infobox key:value content leaked into stored text as raw syntax (`{\"@type`, `application/ld+json`, stray `{...}` braces) versus being cleanly rendered as prose, and whether image alt-text or caption JSON was duplicated into the body. Caveat: do not use a fixed English stopword/short-line length filter as the sole signal — Hindi headers are often short by nature (सम्पादकीय, विषय-सूची); combine repetition-across-document with shortness, not shortness alone, to avoid English-centric overfiltering that would strip legitimate short Hindi headings/verse lines (the corpus contains poetry — see doc example with दोहा/verse structure — where short repeated refrains are content, not boilerplate; a human audit pass must distinguish these).\n\nSTAGE 6 Extraction confidence/routing: a synthesized per-document score combining Stage 2 boilerplate-marker-hit-rate (web only, or NaN/pdf-flag when unavailable), Stage 4 list/table-flattening flag, Stage 5 repeated-line rate, and a cheap OCR-garble proxy (ratio of isolated Devanagari matra/vowel-sign codepoints not attached to a preceding consonant — a robust, script-aware OCR-noise signal, computed via a regex requiring every dependent vowel sign U+093E–U+094C and virama U+094D to be immediately preceded by a consonant U+0915–U+0939/U+0958–U+095F).
